summary_en: Nihon M&A Center Holdings completed acquisition of AI Brain Partners (AIBP) through stock acquisition on October 1, 2026, and simplified share exchange effective November 2, 2026, making AIBP a wholly-owned subsidiary. 250,000 treasury shares were allocated to AIBP shareholders; no new shares were issued.
title_en: Notice regarding Completion of Stock Acquisition of AI Brain Partners Inc. and Full Subsidiary Status through Simplified Share Exchange
translation_en_brief: Nihon M&A Center Holdings Inc. completed its acquisition of AI Brain Partners Inc. (AIBP), making it a wholly-owned subsidiary through a two-step process. On October 1, 2026, the company acquired shares in AIBP to secure a 67.0% voting interest and establish it as a consolidated subsidiary. Subsequently, on November 2, 2026, the company executed a simplified share exchange under the Companies Act Article 796(2), acquiring the remaining shares and achieving 100.0% ownership without requiring shareholder approval. The exchange involved allocation of 250,000 shares of Nihon M&A Center Holdings to AIBP shareholders, all funded by the company's treasury shares; no new shares were issued. AIBP's representatives, Representative Director Shohei Nakamura and Director Masaru Yamamura, became shareholders and continue to manage the subsidiary. AIBP, based in Tokyo's Marunouchi district, operates in AI and BPO implementation, enterprise-wide AI transformation consulting, AI advisory services for management, and AI training. The acquisition aims to integrate AIBP's expertise in AI agent implementation and organizational integration to enhance productivity within the Nihon M&A Center group and to provide customers with comprehensive AI adoption and utilization support throughout the M&A process. AIBP has been consolidated from October 1, 2026, and will be included in consolidated results from the third quarter of fiscal year ended March 2027. The transaction is expected to have minimal impact on fiscal 2027 results; no goodwill is expected to arise from the additional share acquisition, which will be accounted for as a transaction with non-controlling shareholders through changes in capital surplus.
